history.dynasty: Chola (traditional; Imperial Chola contributions late 10th-11th c.; Kanaka Sabha by Madurai Nayaks, 17th c.)
history.period: 2nd century CE per tradition (attributed to Karikala Chola; the standing architecture is later - verify)
history.summary: The Arulmigu Perur Patteeswaraswamy Temple at Perur on the banks of the Noyyal is one of the most revered Shiva temples of western Tamil Nadu (Kongu Nadu). Tradition holds it was built in the 2nd century by Karikala Chola, though this attribution is disputed and the standing structure shows later Chola and Vijayanagara work, with Imperial Chola contributions in the late 10th and early 11th centuries. The name 'Patteeswarar' comes from Tamil 'patti' (cow/calf): Kamadhenu's calf is said to have discovered the swayambhu (self-manifested) lingam, worshipping it with milk. The temple is counted among the places where Shiva performed the Ananda Thandavam. Its fame rests on the architecture: the Kanaka Sabha (built in the 17th century by Alagadri Nayak of the Madurai Nayaks) houses a golden statue of Nataraja, its ceiling carries a network of carved stone chains, and its pillars are carved with Shiva in his many forms - which is why the temple is also called Melai Chidambaram ('the western Chidambaram'), the name used on its official HR&CE site. Notable natural curiosities: the 'Piravapuli' birth-less tamarind whose seeds do not germinate, and the 'Irava Panai' palms said to be over 1,000 years old - hence the epithet 'Pirappu, Irappu illa sthalam' (the place of no birth, no death). The temple is a famous wedding venue and runs an Annadhanam scheme; it is administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE Department.

name: Perur Pateeswarar Temple
town: Perur (CSV town 'Coimbatore' - the temple is at Perur on the Noyyal, ~7 km southwest of Coimbatore city)
town_description: Perur is a suburban temple town ~7 km southwest of Coimbatore city, on the banks of the Noyyal river, known almost entirely for the Patteeswarar Temple and its Bharatanatyam dance tradition. Coimbatore ('Kovai'), Tamil Nadu's second city, is the 'Manchester of South India' - a major textile, engineering and education hub at the foot of the Western Ghats, with a pleasant climate and busy town-bus and suburban rail network.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. Maha Shivaratri (February-March) and Panguni Uthiram (March-April, car festival) are the grandest festivals but very crowded; September brings the Natyanjali classical-dance festival.
